messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 PAGING — GPU pool 'g-pool-west' near exhaustion; free_gpus=2; autoscaler not reacting. alert: INC-2026-042
maia: I'm paged, on it. what's the impact?
samir: Prometheus scrape to infer-west is timing out, prometheus-adapter serving 500s to the API. HPA custom metrics gap since 2026-06-12T09:00:00Z
support-bot: customer 7892 and 9011 reported elevated 504s starting ~08:58 UTC; ticket #TI-4817 opened
mike: checking adapter logs — getting `504 upstream read timeout` from prometheus, and adapter stacktrace `panic: write: broken pipe`
maia: queue length for gpu-worker is climbing: 1200 pending tasks, throttle rate kicking in -> requests queued at the edge
lena: oncall note: we've seen this pattern before when prometheus hits cardinality spike. can we fallback HPA to CPU/queue-length metric?
samir: HPA is configured only on custom metric `gpu/free_count`. since that's missing, HPA froze at 12 replicas.
maia: live-mitigation plan:
 1) restart prometheus-adapter
 2) temporarily increase HPA maxReplicas
 3) scale gpu-worker manually to buy time
 4) failover HPA to `metrics.k8s.io` (cpu) if adapter doesn't recover
 5) throttle non-prod/low-priority routes
maia: executing step 1
```bash
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter
``` 
maia: adapter restarting (rolling) — restarting pods 1/3
devops-bot: action logged: restart triggered by maia
mike: while adapter restarts, I'm scaling gpu-worker and patching HPA
```bash
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gpu-worker --replicas=48
kubectl -n inference patch hpa/gpu-worker -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":80}}'
``` 
mike: scale command accepted; new pods provisioning (expected ~5m to hit GPUs)
julia: heads-up, manual scale will increase billed capacity; notifying finance later
lena: I'll start routing rules to deprioritize non-pay-tier traffic — applying traffic split
maia: support, please inform customers on impacted endpoints and that we're mitigating: short note OK
support-bot: prepared customer update draft: "We are experiencing degraded performance for hosted inference in us-west due to metrics pipeline issues. Our engineers are actively mitigating and expect recovery in ~10-20 minutes."
samir: prometheus-adapter pods stable now but errors persist; `/api/v1/query` latency still high ~3s
maia: fallback: changing HPA to target CPU metric for now
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch hpa/gpu-worker --type='json' -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/metrics/0","value":{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"type":"Utilization","averageUtilization":50}}}}]'
``` 
mike: patched HPA to CPU target — HPA should now be able to scale on node pressure if needed
lena: observing queue trend; started draining a handful of low-priority deployments by setting `replica=0` to free GPUs
julia: on-call handoff in 30m to NOC — leaving notes in pager duty. @maia can you capture decision log?
maia: logging timeline and mitigation steps in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042 (private)
support-bot: sent customer update to affected list (IDs: 7892,9011,9022)
mike: new gpu-worker pods coming up and attaching; free_gpus reported rising to 8
samir: prometheus scrape back to normal baseline; adapter returning metrics again. HPA custom metric `gpu/free_count` is back with recent samples
maia: I'm reverting HPA to original custom metric and lowering maxReplicas back after stabilization
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch hpa/gpu-worker --type='json' -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/metrics/0","value":{"type":"Object","object":{"metric":{"name":"gpu/free_count"},"describedObject":{"kind":"Deployment","name":"gpu-worker","apiVersion":"apps/v1"},"target":{"type":"Value","value":"10"}}}}]'
kubectl -n inference patch hpa/gpu-worker -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":30}}'
``` 
maia: monitoring p50 latency returning to baseline; queue draining: pending 140 -> 30
julia: handing off to night oncall @lena in 20 minutes with notes; incident severity reduced to SEV-2
maia: postmortem tasks: investigate prometheus scrape pressure root cause, add adapter alert on high scrape latency, implement HPA backup metric and automated fallback, document runbook
support-bot: customers notified of resolution and ticket auto-updated to resolved when system stabilized
maia: closing thread in 1h after postmortem doc published
lena: ack, keeping watch; will escalate if flares
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — GPU pool stabilized and autoscaling restored. duration ~55m. tags: gpu, autoscale, prometheus-adapter
